answer: Each identity may curate only one knoll archive, identified by the merkle root of an exclusive specimen list. A specimen is admitted only as a basalt thin-section whose optical-orientation hash is unused in any archive; a colliding section is refused and the deposit posted with it is slashed from the submitting archive. Catalog entries must follow a spiral rule: each new section is filed in the next empty radial bucket (distance from the knoll datum, then bearing), and skipping or repeating a bucket already claimed by another archive voids the entry as copied work.
